questions.question: You created test scripts from requirements and maintained a Requirements Verification Traceability Matrix for Navy programs. How would you use that requirements discipline to define acceptance criteria and quality gates for a multi-team Agile release?

Describe the automation testing you set up for five stand-alone programs at SURVICE: what tools and language(s) did you use, what was automated, and how did you maintain or evaluate the tests over time?

This role requires hands-on C++ and Java/J2EE development. Please walk us through the most substantial C++ and Java work you have personally delivered, including your design choices, testing approach, and your level of ownership.

What is your practical experience with automated unit testing, test-driven development, continuous integration, and source-control workflows? Where your experience is limited, how would you build proficiency quickly for a GitHub- and SonarCloud-based development organization?

You have used Jira for manual testing and bug tracking and modified Team Foundation Server. How would you configure and govern Jira, GitHub, Confluence, and quality reporting so several Scrum teams have transparent backlog, release, and defect status?

Tell us about a time you found a software or hardware issue while verifying a Navy system against requirements. How did you isolate the problem, communicate it to developers or stakeholders, and verify the eventual resolution?

As an Army team leader for six personnel, how did you assign work, maintain accountability, and address a performance or morale challenge? How would that approach need to change when managing and mentoring 15–20 software professionals?

Imagine you are asked to act as Scrum of Scrums Master while two teams have conflicting dependencies and a release date is at risk. What cadence, artifacts, escalation path, and decisions would you use to restore a credible release plan?

The role focuses on Intelligent Transportation Systems, V2X, control systems, and standards such as NTCIP, SAE, and IEEE, which are not shown in your profile. How would you structure your first 90 days to gain sufficient domain knowledge to make sound technical and management decisions?

Your background includes mission-oriented Navy systems, classified-material work, and Security+ certification. What motivates your move from test engineering toward a software development management role in the connected-vehicle/ITS domain, and how would you establish credibility with senior developers and customers?
